verdict.label: HOLD — PCE In-Line; AAPL/MSFT Memory Pass-Through Confirms AI Demand; Russell Recon Tomorrow
verdict.rationale_short: May PCE printed headline 4.1% (in-line) and core 3.4% (1 bp above 3.3% consensus) — exactly the morning brief's 'broadly in-line → HOLD maintained' scenario. SPX finished at 7,357.49 (-0.01%). The session's defining development: Apple announced price increases on iPhone, iPad, and Mac citing higher memory costs; Microsoft raised Xbox prices on the same rationale. AAPL fell ~6.5% and MSFT fell 5.1% to $354.32, while MU closed at $1,165.94 (above premarket $1,083 washout). GDP Q1 third estimate revised up to 2.1% annualized from 1.6% — the mild hawkish add-on the morning brief flagged. The 30Y fell 8 bps to 4.848% despite in-line PCE, expanding the buffer to the 5.00% trigger from 7 bps to 15.2 bps. Regime improving but not cleared. Russell Reconstitution at June 26 close is tomorrow's dominant structural event.

bear_case: The in-line PCE print (core 3.4% — above 3.3% consensus, not below) represents persistent above-comfort-zone inflation for the second consecutive month. The GDP upward revision to 2.1% removes the 'weak growth = Fed caution' narrative — a stronger economy with persistent inflation maximizes the Fed's justification for BofA's September hike. AAPL and MSFT raising consumer hardware prices citing memory costs is not just a bullish AI memory signal; it is a consumer price inflation signal that flows directly into June and July CPI. BTC hitting an intraday low of $59,334 while SPX sits effectively unchanged confirms underlying risk appetite is deteriorating, not improving. Three consecutive sessions below 7,460 with VIX above 17 and DXY above 100 has converted 7,460 from support to resistance. Institutions may use Russell Reconstitution liquidity on June 26 to reduce gross exposure into quarter-end rather than add it. If SPX closes below 7,300 after the June 26 close, HOLD reverts to STEP ASIDE and the BEARISH framework extends into Q3. Invalidation: SPX closes above 7,460 AND VIX closes below 17 simultaneously on any session before June 30.
